narration.say: Boston Dynamics put scooter wheels on its Atlas robot.
Why would a walking robot need wheels?
It doesn't. It's a stress test for its motors.
No motor gives full torque at full speed.
Every launch, turn and stop pushes that limit.
It trained in simulation, where perfect motors teach impossible moves.
So the team measured the real motors, and simulated those.
A robot's AI is only as good as its motor model.
cues: as good as its motor model.

shots.beat: hook: paper humanoid on scooter wheels rolls in and lands a 360 spin jump
super hook: close-up, the foot comes off and a scooter rim + one adapter bolts onto the ankle
answer: shell turns translucent, the actuators glow as it launches hard — a motor stress test
mechanism: torque-speed chart builds; the full-torque-at-full-speed corner is out of reach
proof: launch, turn and stop each push the operating point onto the limit line
it trained in simulation: a grid of ghost robots rolling
constraint: ideal-motor box vs the real triangle; a move in the corner is impossible
fix: measured points from a motor on a test bench; the simulated envelope snaps onto them
payoff: the robot rolls, dashes sideways and stops cleanly
